prompt:
A 1000 kg car traveling at 20 m/s crashes head-on and comes to a complete stop. Consider two scenarios: (1) the car has an airbag, extending the collision time to 0.1 s, and (2) the car has no airbag, and the collision time is only 0.02 s.

**(a)** Calculate the impulse delivered to the car during the crash. (Note: this value is the same in both scenarios.)

**(b)** Calculate the average force on the car in Scenario 1 (with the airbag).

**(c)** Calculate the average force on the car in Scenario 2 (without the airbag), and compare it to your answer from part (b).

rubric.description: Correctly computes the impulse J = Δp = mΔv = 20,000 N·s
Correctly applies F=J/Δt with Δt=0.1s to get F=200,000 N
Correctly applies F=J/Δt with Δt=0.02s to get F=1,000,000 N
Correctly notes that the force without the airbag is 5 times larger, illustrating why extending collision time (with an airbag) reduces the force for the same impulse

sampleResponse:
(a) J = Δp = mΔv = (1000)(20-0) = 20,000 N·s.
(b) F = J/Δt = 20,000/0.1 = 200,000 N.
(c) F = J/Δt = 20,000/0.02 = 1,000,000 N. This is 5 times larger than the airbag scenario -- since the impulse (change in momentum) is the same in both cases, spreading it over a longer time (with the airbag) results in a much smaller average force.

prompt:
A 5 kg cart moving at 8 m/s collides with a stationary 3 kg cart. The two carts stick together (perfectly inelastic collision).

**(a)** Calculate the combined velocity of the two carts after the collision.

**(b)** Calculate the total kinetic energy of the system before the collision.

**(c)** Calculate the total kinetic energy of the system after the collision, and determine how much kinetic energy was lost.

rubric.description: Correctly applies conservation of momentum to find v_f = 5 m/s
Correctly computes KE before the collision as 160 J
Correctly computes KE after the collision as 100 J
Correctly computes the kinetic energy lost as 60 J

sampleResponse:
(a) Momentum conservation: (5)(8)+(3)(0) = (5+3)v_f, so 40 = 8v_f, giving v_f = 5 m/s.
(b) KE_before = (1/2)(5)(8^2) = (1/2)(5)(64) = 160 J.
(c) KE_after = (1/2)(8)(5^2) = (1/2)(8)(25) = 100 J. Kinetic energy lost = 160 - 100 = 60 J (converted to heat/sound/deformation during the collision).

prompt:
Two objects lie on the x-axis: $m_1 = 3$ kg at $x=0$ m, and $m_2 = 5$ kg at $x=8$ m.

**(a)** Calculate the x-coordinate of the system's center of mass.

**(b)** Explain, without recalculating, whether the center of mass would be closer to $m_1$ or farther from $m_1$ if $m_2$'s mass were increased (with positions unchanged).

**(c)** If the two objects are connected by a spring and pushed apart (with no external horizontal force on the system), what happens to the position of the center of mass as they move? Explain your reasoning.

rubric.description: Correctly reasons that increasing m2's mass would shift the center of mass farther from m1 (closer to m2), since the weighted average shifts toward the larger mass
Correctly states that the center of mass stays at the same position (x=5 m) as the objects move apart
Correctly explains this using the fact that the spring force is internal to the system, and with no external horizontal force, the center of mass cannot accelerate

sampleResponse:
(a) x_cm = (m1x1+m2x2)/(m1+m2) = (3(0)+5(8))/(3+5) = 40/8 = 5 m.
(b) Increasing m2's mass would shift the center of mass farther from m1 (closer to m2, i.e., to a larger x-value), since the center of mass formula weights each position by its mass -- a larger m2 pulls the weighted average more strongly toward x2.
(c) The center of mass remains at x=5 m as the objects move apart. The spring force pushing them apart is internal to the system (an action-reaction pair), and with no external horizontal force acting on the system, the center of mass cannot accelerate -- it stays fixed even as the two masses move in opposite directions.
